what: Why the input-based OOD detector fires on downstream stations at operating percentiles 50 and 75 in design M -- for BOTH gravity states.
method: Distance-to-training self-scores of the design-M TRAINING rows (each training point is its own nearest neighbour), thresholded at the given percentile, tallied by x/D band. Uses training inputs only; no test output, error or PhysMAP result enters it.
reading: Training stations are log-spaced, but the detector measures raw x_over_D, so downstream stations are the sparsest part of the grid and carry the largest self-scores. At low percentiles the detector fires on the TRAINING data itself there. A test input identical to one of those rows fires for the same reason. That is its built-in alarm pattern, not buoyancy detection: the output is identical with gravity off, where those stations are accurate to 0.03 %.
predeclared: PREDECLARE_design_M_matched.md states lower percentiles are reported but do not decide, for exactly this reason. This file measures the mechanism; it changes no criterion.
